page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g9a.24xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance based on the KVM hypervisor. The hardware profile is built around an AMD EPYC 9T25 processor operating on the x86_64 architecture at 2.7 GHz. The system provides 96 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 384.0 GB of memory, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The server does not include GPU accelerators.

The instance does not include bundled local storage, meaning all persistence depends on network-attached block storage devices. It supports high-capacity network connectivity with a baseline bandwidth of 48 Gbps, accommodating high-traffic inter-service communication. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not provided by default with this profile.

Given its scale, the hardware density favors large-scale parallel processing where balanced per-core memory is sufficient. The primary operational tradeoff is its dependence on remote storage interfaces for disk operations, necessitating proper network volume sizing. The configuration is suitable for large-scale web serving, enterprise application backends, batch data processing, and distributed database services.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g9a.24xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the AMD EPYC 9T25 processor on the x86_64 architecture. Delivered through the KVM hypervisor, it provides 96 dedicated vCPUs clocked at 2.7 GHz paired with 384.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:4 resource ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The server does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators, directing disk I/O to external storage volumes supported by a 48 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. With no complimentary public IPv4 addresses included, network connectivity operates through cloud-managed IP configurations. The instance delivers high parallel processing density and memory headroom, making it appropriate for multi-tiered enterprise application deployments, large-scale web servers, continuous integration pipelines, batch processing, and distributed transactional databases.
